problems.stem: Which statement best matches Mayer's dual-channel assumption?
options: The brain processes all information through one shared channel
Visual and auditory information are processed through separate channels
Only text can support deep learning
problems.explanation: Mayer's theory assumes separate visual and auditory channels, each with limited capacity.

problems.stem: Why can spoken narration paired with graphics sometimes outperform graphics plus dense on-screen text?
options: Because narration uses the auditory channel and can reduce overload in the visual channel
Because learners never read text carefully
Because text is always an inferior medium
Because images automatically teach all concepts
problems.explanation: The modality effect matters because distributing processing across channels can reduce overload when designed well.

problems.stem: Which design choice best applies the coherence principle?
options: Adding dramatic music and decorative animations unrelated to the lesson
Removing seductive but irrelevant media elements that do not support the learning goal
Presenting every possible detail so nothing is omitted
Duplicating narration as full paragraphs on the screen
problems.explanation: The coherence principle recommends removing unnecessary material that consumes attention without supporting the objective.

problems.stem: A simulation includes narration, identical on-screen paragraphs, three flashing callouts, and background music. What is the most likely instructional problem?
options: The design is likely generating cognitive overload through extraneous processing
The design has too little engagement
The problem is only that there is no grading rubric
problems.explanation: Too many simultaneous media elements can overload working memory and reduce learning rather than increase it.
